newsitem.title: UK: Merrill says coffee rally may last till September.
newsitem.headline: Merrill says coffee rally may last till September.

text.p: Coffee prices could stay firm at least until New York's September expiry, given the lack of supplies even though there is no Brazilian frost, U.S. brokerage Merrill Lynch said in a report.
Coffee has rallied sharply since the beginning of this year on persistent tightness in physical supplies.
"We would look for the uptrend to continue," Merrill said in its biweekly Commodity Market Trends report.
"Relief from the high prices is not likely to come before July," the broker said.

"Seasonally the market generally retreats from mid-July onwards if there is no frost in Brazil, but given the lack of availability the market might stay firm even for the September expiration," it added.
It said this was especially if the 1997/98 crop in Colombia was going to be delayed as Colombian sources predicted, it said.
September, which expires on September 18, was last traded at 179.50 cents a lb on Tuesday, up from 111.75 cents on January 2. It hit a contract high of 184 cents on April 25.
The danger months for Brazilian coffee are June and July and the last crop-damaging frosts in 1994 sent world prices sky-rocketing.
Merrill said the brisk pace of sales in the first quarter of this year had left exporters with only minimal amounts of fresh coffee and stocks to sell in the duration of the current season.
"We estimate a total shortfall in availability between this (second) quarter and the next of about three million bags," it said.
